Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

couple noun

two people together: a married couple, partners

also married couple, a young couple, husband and wife, they’re a couple

classical

Catull. 61.225–226: at, bonī conjugēs, bene vīvite

conjūnx, conjugis m./f.

noun, third declension; in the plural, conjugēs, a married couple

a spouse; in the plural, husband and wife

Lewis & Short: in the plural for the married pair (Catull. 61, 66). See spouse.

Other words

  • pār, paris n. — a pair: two who belong together

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 15: vix tria aut quattuor nōminantur paria amīcōrum; Ov. Met. 13.833: pār columbārum (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: a pair, a couple, of people or animals.

  • marītī, marītōrum m. pl. — married people, husband and wife

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · post-classical · Apul. Met. 8 (Lewis & Short): novī marītī, a young couple; Dig. 24.1.52 (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short mark this plural post-classical: the jurists and Apuleius.

Examples

  • lūsimus satis. at, bonī conjugēs, bene vīvite

    we have played enough. And you, good husband and wife, live happilyCatull. 61.225–226

  • ex omnibus saeculīs vix tria aut quattuor nōminantur paria amīcōrum

    from all the ages hardly three or four pairs of friends are namedCic. Amic. 15

See also spouse, husband, wife, couple, pair.

SourcesLewis & Short: conjunx · Lewis & Short: par · Lewis & Short: maritus
